description: C transaction ownership scope and fresh-query qualification
qualification: normal local combined-source Linux node and ephemeral demo trust

initialFailure.diagnostic: A separate instrumented node observed the trap before state-acquisition host entry. The template had left its ownership scope at a zero-byte limit, so its first state-handle adoption could not succeed.

observations: The C transaction template now initializes its bounded ownership scope before state acquisition and requests finite capacity for transaction codec scratch and cold startup.

The maintained C compiler produced the corrected component; the explicit transaction demo signer accepted its completed observed build and linked companion. The Rust-only demo mode rejected this C build before creating output.

The normal node admitted the C release. An authenticated fresh query returned count zero and an absent key; command count stayed zero. Node state and effect owners retired physically and shutdown was clean.
The local signer example suite passed 47 tests and C authoring tests passed eight tests.
limitations: The copied local fixture observation retains an obsolete Rust label; the signed service, C build type, captured C source and component identify this as the C guest.
This is one C fresh query, not a successful command or intent, rejection, cancellation, crash, memory-limit or full language qualification.
The normal node uses a local verified combined-source snapshot containing unmerged work and short-lived demo trust; hosted CI and installed distribution remain separate.
